docs.title: Momo documentation
docs.text:
Momo is a Go ORM that generates typed column and relation descriptors from plain Go structs, keeps SQL explicit and inspectable, builds pgvector support into the core API, and ships its own migration engine that writes reviewable SQL. It supports PostgreSQL with pgvector; capabilities states exactly what else exists and what does not. Pages are written from the code and checked in CI: every Go block compiles, and the examples run against PostgreSQL.

New here? Start with getting started.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
• Getting started: requirements, install, a first program that talks to PostgreSQL, and where the typed API starts.
  • Guide for AI coding agents: one self-contained file for an agent using Momo in an application: setup, modeling, migrations, queries, relations, vectors, errors, testing, known pitfalls and rules. Also indexed by llms.txt at the repository root.
  • Go to SQL type mapping: column type per Go type, edge values, null handling.
  • Vector search: pgvector types, metrics, limits, search settings and the binary codec.
  • MySQL and MariaDB: supported servers, DSN requirements, the capability matrix, write and locking differences, error mapping, and what is not available yet.
  • Full-text search: the tsvector column type, the match, query, rank and headline builders, and a hybrid vector plus text ranking pattern.
  • Projections: declaring a projection, From and Columns, the generated metadata, tuple rows (Row1 to Row10), the soft-delete filter.
  • Relations: declaring, loading, filtering and writing relations, with error behavior and limits.
  • Migration safety and recovery: snapshots, apply semantics, locks, failure recovery, production checklist, CLI reference.
  • Importing models from other ORMs: the GORM, Bun and Ent readers (static, they never execute your code), the import report and what each report kind means; the momo import command is not wired yet.
  • Read replicas: WithReplicas, which statements go to a replica, reading your own writes, and what happens when a replica is down.
  • Testing applications: the momotest kit: a schema or a rolled-back transaction per test, migrations applied, fixture seeding, parallel-safe.
  • Interceptors: application-level per-handle rules that add predicates or deny typed statements, the tenant recipe, and the paths they do not cover (not a security boundary).
  • Static check for raw SQL: the momovet analyzer that reports non-constant SQL passed to the raw-SQL functions.
  • Interceptors: WithInterceptor statement rules per handle, a tenant-handle recipe, and every path an interceptor does not cover.
  • momovet: the static analyzer that reports raw SQL built with + or a format call.
  • Capabilities: what each database supports, what is not built, and what returns ErrUnsupported.
  • Performance: the measured hook-overhead allocation budget and the layout of the comparison benchmark suite.
  • Supported versions: Go, PostgreSQL, pgvector, PgBouncer, pgx and OS versions in CI for v0.3.0, and the stability policy.
  • Using these docs with an AI coding agent: where an agent should read, canonical patterns and a copy-paste AGENTS.md snippet.
  • Architecture: the package layering, dependency rules and contracts the code follows.
  • Contributing: prerequisites, test commands, commit messages and file headers.

docs.text:
Runnable programs, each tested end to end in CI. See the examples index for the layout and how to add one.

  • quickstart: the root README loop: models, generate, CRUD, relations, vector search, a transaction.
  • crud-zero-null: insert, update, delete; zero value versus NULL versus default; soft delete.
  • transactions: Tx, rollback, savepoints, read-only and isolation, retry on serialization failure.
  • testing: momotest: a database or a rolled-back transaction per test, migrations applied, seeded fixtures, parallel tests.
  • relations: has-many, belongs-to, many-to-many; Load, Preload, Joined, Has, Link, CreateGraph.
  • projection-pagination: column subsets, keyset pagination with a tie-break, counting.
  • vector-search: HNSW index, nearest-neighbour queries, filters, search settings.
  • upgrade-database: change a model after production: add a column with a default, add an index, rename a column, apply with data kept, generate --check and drift.
  • custom-sql-migration: hand-written SQL migrations beside generated ones: backfill, DO $$ splitting, -- momo:no-transaction, a hand-written CONCURRENTLY index, momo.sum checksums.
  • adopt-existing-schema: put a plain-SQL database under Momo with migrate baseline (momo generate --from-db can then write the models from the database).

docs.title: Momo architecture and contracts
docs.text:
This is the contract for every implementation plan under .procoder/plans/. Plans and code use the names below exactly; changing a name means changing this file first. Requirements live in .procoder/specs/momo.md (cited as S-n).

The package and contract sections exist in the code today, except what the section "Planned, not implemented" lists. PostgreSQL through pgx has the only migration dialect; drivers also exist for SQLite (driver/sqlitedriver, cgo, not on Windows) and for MySQL and MariaDB (driver/mysqldriver), with no migrations or vector builders on those. Anything listed as planned has no code yet, and no other document may describe it as available. The sections "Delivery order" and "Ownership decisions" are roadmap and plan bookkeeping, not status: they describe intended order and ownership, and do not show what has been built.

docs.title: Layering
docs.text:
cmd/momo (CLI)
                 │
   ┌─────────────┼──────────────┐
   gen (plugin interface; gen/viz and gen/apiquery ship)
   │     migrate ── migrate/postgres
   │        │
   └──── schema ◄──────────────┐
            ▲                  │
   momo (root runtime) ── dialect, vector, types
            ▲
   driver/pgxdriver

Dependency rules (enforced by TestImportGraph, which runs go list -deps):

  1. momo, dialect, schema, vector, types import only the standard library and each other. No driver, no x/tools, no YAML.
  2. driver/* import momo plus their database driver only.
  3. gen, migrate/*, cmd/* may import x/tools, YAML and drivers. Application binaries that import only momo + one driver never link them.
  4. Generated code imports only momo, vector, types, schema and the model package.

docs.title: dialect
docs.text:
• type Name string; constants Postgres = "postgres", SQLite = "sqlite", MySQL = "mysql".
  • type Flavor string; FlavorMySQL = "mysql", FlavorMariaDB = "mariadb" (set on MySQL dialects only).
  • type Dialect struct with fields Name, Flavor, MaxParams, and capability booleans Returning, OnConflict, OnDuplicateKey, Locking, NullsOrdering, DefaultInUpdate, DefaultInValues, RecursiveCTE, RowValues, Savepoints, IsolationLevels, TransactionalDDL, ILike, Merge, WindowFunctions.
  • func For(n Name) *Dialect, func MySQLFlavor(f Flavor) *Dialect.
  • Methods: AppendPlaceholder(b []byte, n int) []byte, AppendIdent(b []byte, ident string) []byte (MySQL uses backticks), QuoteIdent(string) string.

docs.title: schema
docs.text:
• Types as in schema/schema.go: Schema{FormatVersion, Dialect, Schemas, Extensions, Enums, Tables, Views, Functions, Triggers, Policies}, Table, Column, Unique, Index, IndexPart, KV, ForeignKey, Check.
  • const FormatVersion = 1. func Load(r io.Reader) (*Schema, error) refuses format_version > FormatVersion with ErrNewerFormat.
  • normalize.go: func NormalizeType(d dialect.Name, t string) string, func NormalizeExpr(d dialect.Name, e string) string, func Equal(a, b *Schema) bool.

docs.title: momo (root runtime)
docs.text:
• Handles: type DB, type Tx, sealed type Querier interface{ Dialect() *dialect.Dialect; conn() *execer }. func New(drv Driver, opts ...Option) *DB.
  • Driver contract: Driver, DriverTx, Rows, TxOptions{Isolation sql.IsolationLevel; ReadOnly bool}; optional ErrorClassifier{ClassifyError(error) error}, Pinner{Pin(ctx) (PinnedConn, error)}, Copier{CopyFrom(ctx, table string, cols []string, rows [][]any) (int64, error)}, Batcher{SendBatch(ctx, []Compiled) ([]Rows, error)}, PoolStater{PoolStats() PoolStats}.
  • SQL building: Builder, Compiled{SQL string; Args []any}, Expr, Expression[T], Predicate = Expression[bool], ColumnRef, Orderable, Order, Nulls, Subquery, TableSource, TableRef{Name, Alias, Schema}.
  • Aliases and joins: Column.As(alias) re-qualifies a column; AsExpr() returns it as an Expression[T]. Each SELECT records the qualifiers its FROM and JOIN sources expose, and a column qualified by any other table is an ErrValidation at build time (a reference to an enclosing SELECT, as in a correlated subquery, is allowed).
  • Columns: Column[T], NullColumn[T], VectorColumn[V], constructors NewColumn[T] (table, name string, flags uint16), NewNullColumn[T], NewVectorColumn[V]. Flags FlagPK, FlagUnique, FlagNullable, FlagIdentity, FlagReadOnly, FlagVersion, FlagSoftDelete, FlagHasDefault, FlagCreateOnly, FlagImmutable, FlagSensitive, FlagCreatedAt, FlagUpdatedAt.
  • Writes: Assignment (from Column.Set/SetExpr/SetDefault/SetExcluded, NullColumn.SetNull).
  • Metadata: Model and Projection markers, ColumnMeta{Name; Flags uint16}, Meta[T]{Table, Schema string; Columns; Ptr func(*T,int) any; Value func(*T,int) any; TableSchema *schema.Table; Identity, Version, SoftDelete int; SoftDeleteKind; CreatedAt, UpdatedAt int; PK []int; Fields []FieldHook[T]}, Modeler[T] (*T with MomoMeta() *Meta[T]).
  • Queries: Select[T, PT Modeler[T]] (q Querier) SelectQuery[T], Insert[T, PT] (q) InsertQuery[T], Update[T, PT] (q) UpdateQuery[T], Delete[T, PT] (q) DeleteQuery[T], SoftDelete[T, PT] (q) UpdateQuery[T], Exec(ctx, q, sql, args...) (int64, error). There is no typed raw query; RawSubquery and the placeholders below cover raw SQL inside a statement. All query values are immutable; methods return modified copies.
  • Subqueries and CTEs: SelectQuery is a Subquery (IN, EXISTS, select-list scalar); With and WithRecursive add CTEs whose names are in scope for the whole statement, so a recursive CTE can reference itself; Union(all, ...), FromSubquery(q, alias) and CTE(name) cover set operations and ad-hoc sources; RawSubquery(sql, args...) is the raw-SELECT escape hatch (verbatim trusted SQL, ? binds). Scope checks never reject these shapes.
  • Terminals on SelectQuery[T]: All, One, First, Each, Iter, Count, Exists, SQL; on mutations: Exec(ctx) (Result, error), SQL(). type Result struct{ RowsAffected int64 }.
  • Relations (see relations.md): generated Relation[P, C] descriptors (relation.go; the generator emits one value per relation field, with key accessors, Through for many-to-many and Discriminator for polymorphic relations). Loading: Load[P, C] (parents, one relation, then opts ...LoadOption[C]) and LoadAll[P] (parents, then loaders ...Loader[P]), both taking a context and a Querier first and returning an error. Loader[P] is a sealed interface implemented by Relation itself, RelationLoader (returned by Relation.Scope(opts ...LoadOption[C]) and Relation.Then(nested ...Loader[C]), which chain: rel.Scope(...).Then(...)) and Relation.Joined(); options are LoadWhere, LoadOrderBy, LoadPerParentLimit, LoadWithDeleted, LoadOnlyDeleted. SelectQuery.Preload(loaders ...Loader[T]) runs the loads after the rows are read, and joined loaders fold into the parent statement. On a Batcher connection (pgx) the statements of one LoadAll level are pipelined in one round trip. Predicates and traversal: Has, HasFrom, HasNo, CountOrder(Direction), From. Writes: Link, Unlink, Replace, Count, Include with CreateGraph, FindOrCreate, UpsertByPK. Observability: RelationHook and RelationEvent. With stays the CTE method.
  • Transactions: DB.Tx(ctx, TxOptions, func(*Tx) error) error, DB.Begin, Tx.Commit/Rollback/Tx/Savepoint/RollbackTo/Release; DB.AdoptTx(DriverTx) binds a Tx to a caller-owned transaction (Commit and Rollback return ErrAdoptedTx), Tx.DriverTx() exposes the driver transaction.
  • Observability: Hook, an interface with BeforeQuery (takes a context and a query event, returns a context) and AfterQuery (takes a context and a query event), QueryEvent, options WithHook, WithArgLogging, WithClock (takes a function returning the current time), WithMaxParams.
  • Errors (errors.go): Error{Kind, Op, Table, Column, Constraint, Err} plus Detail() string; sentinels ErrNotFound, ErrTooManyRows, ErrUniqueViolation, ErrForeignKeyViolation, ErrCheckViolation, ErrNotNullViolation, ErrSerialization, ErrOptimisticLock, ErrUnsupported, ErrUnfilteredMutation, ErrTxDone, ErrAdoptedTx, ErrInvalidVector (= vector.ErrInvalidVector), ErrValidation, ErrBusy, ErrLimitExceeded. Migration sentinels live in migrate: ErrChecksumMismatch, ErrDirty, ErrLocked, ErrDestructive, ErrBranchConflict.
  • Placeholders in raw SQL: ? positional, ?? literal ?, @name named (via momo.Named), momo.In(slice) expands, momo.Ident(name) quotes.

docs.title: vector
docs.text:
Vector []float32, HalfVector []float32, SparseVector{Dim int; Indices []int32; Values []float32}, Bits{Len int; Data []byte}; each implements sql.Scanner, driver.Valuer, momo.DialectValuer, Validate(dim int) error. var ErrInvalidVector.

Vector fields declare their dimension with the field tag dim:<n> (e.g. momo:"embedding,dim:1536"). The Go type selects the SQL type: vector, halfvec, sparsevec or bit.

docs.title: types
docs.text: JSON[T], Date, TimeOfDay, UUID, Hstore; each a codec (sql.Scanner + driver.Valuer + SQLType(dialect.Name) string).

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text: • driver/pgxdriver: New(pool *pgxpool.Pool, opts ...Option) momo.Driver; FromSQLDB(db *sql.DB) momo.Driver (pgx stdlib); option WithExecMode(pgx.QueryExecMode); SQLTx(*sql.Tx) and PgxTx(pgx.Tx, opts ...Option) wrap a caller-owned transaction for DB.AdoptTx; UnwrapSQLTx(*momo.Tx) and UnwrapPgxTx(*momo.Tx) return the real transaction.

docs.title: migrate
docs.text:
• Directory format: <YYYYMMDDHHMMSS>_<name>.up.sql, optional .down.sql, <version>_<name>.snapshot.json, momo.sum. Directives: -- momo:no-transaction, -- momo:destructive, -- momo:split. Migrations are forward only: apply never runs a .down.sql file; only Engine.Rollback does.
  • Go API: type Engine struct; NewEngine(drv momo.Driver, dir fs.FS, opts ...Option) (*Engine, error); methods Diff(ctx, desired *schema.Schema, name string, opts DiffOptions) (*Migration, error), Plan(ctx) ([]Pending, error), Apply(ctx, ApplyOptions) (*Report, error), Status(ctx), Baseline(ctx, version string, force bool), Drift(ctx) (*DriftReport, error), Resolve(ctx, version string, state ResolveState), Rehash, Inspect, AutoMigrate(ctx, desired *schema.Schema) (*AutoReport, error); the package function ValidateOffline checks a directory without a database.
  • The PostgreSQL implementation in migrate/postgres satisfies migrate.Dialect (Dialect, Inspect, Render, HistoryDDL, Setup, Lock; see the additions below).
  • The history table momo_migrations is defined by the dialect's HistoryDDL.

docs.title: gen
docs.text:
• gen.Load(patterns []string, cfg Config) (*Graph, []Diagnostic, error) → Graph{Models []*Model; Schema *schema.Schema}; gen.Emit(g *Graph, w *Writer) error; Writer is the only file writer (refuses non-generated targets, gofmt, deterministic).
  • Plugin interface: type Plugin interface{ Name() string; Generate(g *Graph, w *Writer) error }.
  • Generated files start with // Code generated by momo (format 1). DO NOT EDIT. (no momo release version, so upgrading momo does not rewrite generated files; older files that carry a version are still recognised); per-package momo_gen.go in the model package, per-model subpackage <lowercase model name>/momo_gen.go.
  • Writer.Text(path, data) buffers non-Go generated text (Mermaid, DOT, protobuf, GraphQL schema, YAML) under the same refusal rules as File without formatting; the first line of data must be the generated header in the comment style of the format (//, %% or #). Writer.Scaffold(path, data) writes a file only when it does not exist yet: a starting point the user owns, with no header, never overwritten.
  • gen/viz: Edge, EdgesFromGraph, EdgesFromSchema, Tables, TablesFromSchema, Mermaid, DOT, Render and Plugin{Format, Out} (name viz, writes schema.mmd or schema.dot). momo viz [--format mermaid|dot] [--snapshot file] [--out file] draws the models or a migration snapshot; it is a CLI command, not yet selectable from momo.yaml.
  • gen/graphql.SDL(g), gen/grpc.Proto(g, lock, pkg) with the field-number Lock (LoadLock, Assign, Marshal) and gen/openapi.Document(g, opts): pure functions from the model graph to GraphQL SDL, a .proto file and an OpenAPI 3.1 JSON document. They are not yet gen.Plugin implementations and not selectable from momo.yaml or the CLI. The lock is JSON, so it cannot carry the generated header; writing it needs a Writer method that does not exist yet. The lock records retired field names in reserved_names next to the retired numbers; a lock written before that field existed still loads, but a momo build older than the field drops reserved_names when it rewrites the lock, so do not mix builds on one lock.
  • gen/apiquery: request-side helpers shared by the API generators: EncodeCursor/DecodeCursor (opaque base64url keyset cursors), ClampLimit with DefaultLimit 50 and MaxLimit 200, and ParseFilter (a Filter of column, operator and text value resolved through a generated ColumnByName).
  • Config file momo.yaml (parsed in gen/config, shared with the CLI).
  • migrate: section: type config.MigrateConfig owned by momo-02, semantics by momo-04.

docs.title: Other packages
docs.text: cmd/momo (the CLI: generate and migrate) and momotest (the public test kit for applications: a schema or a rolled-back transaction per test with the project migrations applied, and fixture seeding; see testing.md). Every other package once listed here is under "Planned, not implemented".

docs.title: Planned, not implemented
docs.text:
None of the names below exist in the code. They are design intent from the plans and may change or be dropped; do not call them from code or describe them as available in user documentation.

  • Query options and limits: MaxRows, WithMaxInList, and a typed raw query Raw[T, PT] returning RawQuery[T].
  • Interceptors: Interceptor, Operation, WithInterceptor.
  • Read replicas and unit of work: WithReplicas, DB.Replica, NewUnitOfWork, AllowStaleReads; see docs/replicas.md.
  • Generated per-model hook sets: Meta.Hooks as HookSet[T] (today Meta.Fields carries FieldHook[T] only).
  • Read-only view models: marker View (tag momo:"view:<name>[,materialized]"), WritableModeler[T], MomoWritable, and RefreshMaterializedView.
  • Migration engine: Engine.Lint, Engine.Rebase, an online Engine.Validate, and the -- momo:sqlite-foreign-keys-off directive.
  • Other databases: driver/sqlitedriver, driver/sqlitepure, driver/mysqldriver, migrate/sqlite, migrate/mysql and migrate/importers/{atlas,bun,goose,golangmigrate}. Their testopen entries come with them.
  • Tooling packages: momolog (slog hook), momovet and cmd/momovet (analyzer), importer/{gorm,bun,ent} (see importers) and the plugins and handlers of gen/graphql, gen/grpc and gen/openapi (their schema, protobuf and document emitters exist; see Other packages).
  • Separate modules: otelmomo (OpenTelemetry) and bench.

docs.title: Contract additions (round 1, from plan reviews)
docs.text: Each name below is owned by the plan in brackets; that plan's Interfaces: block is the source of truth for its exact signature. Other plans consume the name as written.

docs.title: Root momo
docs.text:
• PinnedConn interface: Query, Exec (same signatures as Driver), Begin(ctx, TxOptions) (DriverTx, error), Release() error; obtained through Pinner.Pin(ctx). Release closes Rows still open, then returns the connection (a repeat after success is a nil no-op); while a Query, Exec or Begin is executing in another goroutine it returns an error matching ErrPinnedBusy and releases nothing. Pinned connections of drivers that can destroy a session also implement the optional Discarder{Discard() error}: it closes the underlying connection and then releases it so the pool destroys it (open Rows closed first; ErrPinnedBusy while a call is in flight; nil when already released or discarded). Callers that cannot restore session state (failed advisory unlock or RESET) call it instead of leaving a dirty connection in the pool. PoolStats struct (acquired, idle, total, wait count, wait duration). Capabilities / CapabilityReporter. Exact Copier and Batcher signatures. [momo-03 Task 1]
  • func (db *DB) OnConn(pc PinnedConn) *DB: a DB bound to one pinned connection that keeps db's hooks, classifier and options. Used for non-transactional Go migrations and session-scoped work. [momo-03]
  • testopen.Each takes the test, a callback, and optional momo options; it passes the options to every available dialect's DB (PostgreSQL and SQLite; SQLite is skipped in a build without cgo or on Windows). [momo-03]
  • WithMaxParams(n) lowers the per-statement bind limit for chunking tests and for databases configured with lower limits. [momo-06]
  • Batcher is implemented by the pgx driver and by pgx transactions. The pgx pool tracer calls the observability recorder for pool wait (RecordPoolWait, owned by momo-09). [momo-03 implements, momo-09 defines] Batch results are buffered eagerly and without bound: SendBatch reads every row of every statement into memory before it returns (so the connection is free and rows can be read in any order), and a failed batch returns one error naming the statement index, never its arguments. With the default QueryExecMode Exec the batch is sent as unnamed extended-protocol statements, so no prepared statement is created (PgBouncer-safe); pgx has no per-batch mode, so any other WithExecMode is accepted only when it equals the pool connection default, else ErrUnsupported. Pinned connections and OnConn handles run COPY and batch on the pinned session.
  • QueryEvent adds PoolWait, InTx, NumArgs, Dialect. [momo-09]
  • WithClock (takes a function returning the current time), ErrBusy, ErrValidation, ErrLimitExceeded. Sentinels are declared in errors.go by momo-01. [momo-05]
  • Meta.Fields holds one FieldHook[T] per column that needs a Go-side default or validator. [momo-05]
  • The Error.Detail method returns the driver detail as a string; driver-level redaction keeps driver detail off the Error text. The compiled statement carries a sensitive-args mask used by hooks: values bound from sensitive columns show as momo.RedactedArg; raw momo.SQL arguments are not masked. [momo-03, momo-05]
  • Tx.SetLocal(ctx, name, value string) error (set_config(name, value, true), transaction-scoped) for RLS and search settings. [momo-04 Task 23]

docs.title: dialect
docs.text: dialect.Dialect carries these capability flags: Returning, InsertReturning, OnConflict, OnDuplicateKey, Locking, NullsOrdering, DefaultInUpdate, DefaultInValues, RecursiveCTE, RowValues, Savepoints, IsolationLevels, TransactionalDDL, ILike, Merge, WindowFunctions, plus Vector (VectorCaps), MaxParams and MaxInList. There are no JSON, Arrays, UpdateFrom or MergeReturning flags. The public momo.Merge builder exists (MergeQuery[T], with Returning); it gates at run time on the server version the driver reports (ServerVersioner, or SELECT server_version_num on a Tx): PostgreSQL 15 or later for MERGE, PostgreSQL 17 or later for MERGE ... RETURNING, else ErrUnsupported. [momo-05]

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text: • pgxdriver.WithExecMode defaults to pgx.QueryExecModeExec (unnamed statements, server-side binding, PgBouncer-safe). QueryExecModeCacheStatement is opt-in, as are QueryExecModeCacheDescribe and QueryExecModeDescribeExec. QueryExecModeSimpleProtocol is rejected, because values must always be bound server-side. PgBouncer transaction pooling uses QueryExecModeExec. pgxdriver.FromConnConfig(cfg *pgx.ConnConfig, opts ...Option) (*sql.DB, momo.Driver). [momo-03]

docs.title: migrate
docs.text:
• migrate.Dialect adds Dialect() *dialect.Dialect, HistoryDDL() []string, Setup(ctx, momo.PinnedConn, SessionOptions) (reset func() error, err error). Lock also reports the holder. There is no global registry: NewEngine requires migrate.WithDialect(d), and the CLI selects the dialect statically. [momo-04]
  • The history table adds apply_id (groups the migrations of one apply run) and kind (sql, or go for a GoMigration). Transactional migrations write their history row inside the migration transaction. Only non-transactional failed/running rows are dirty. [momo-04]
  • Snapshots are stored as a wrapper {format_version, parent, schema}. [momo-04 Task 6]
  • migrate.GoMigration (fields Version, Name, Up, UpNoTx, Checksum) and the option migrate.WithGoMigrations: Go migrations are ordered with the SQL files by version and recorded with kind = 'go'. Up takes a *momo.Tx and runs in the migration transaction; UpNoTx takes a *momo.DB on the pinned connection through OnConn, with the dirty/resolve semantics of a no-transaction SQL file. The recorded checksum is a hash of version, name and the optional Checksum string (code cannot be hashed). A version shared with a SQL file is an error. They exist only in the application's process, so the momo CLI cannot run them; they are forward-only. ValidateOffline takes the registered migrations as extra arguments to check their snapshots. migrate.WithGoMigrationDB supplies the application's *momo.DB for them. Apply returns ErrGoMigrationUnregistered when a snapshot-only version (a Go migration the engine does not have) would be passed by later SQL. RefuseGoRollback and ErrGoMigrationNotReversible are for the rollback code to refuse rows of kind go. See docs/migrations.md section 6a. [issue 43]

docs.title: Generator companion (MomoConfig) methods
docs.text: Index, IndexExpr, Unique, Check, Enum, Default, Comment, Collate take literals and field references. There is no Table method: the table name comes from the marker tag momo:"table:<name>" (momo-02 Task 7). View, Function, Trigger, Policy, RLS, Partition, PartitionOf each take one composite literal of the matching structured schema type owned by momo-04 Task 1 (schema.View covers materialized views through its Materialized field). momo-02 parses them statically; any other form is a diagnostic.

docs.title: Test harness (internal/testdb)
docs.text: The harness returns connection strings only, so driver packages can use it without import cycles: PostgresURL, PostgresAppRoleURL, PgBouncerURL, SQLitePath, MySQL84URL, MySQL97URL, MariaDBURL and Schema, each taking the *testing.T. internal/testdb/testopen opens PostgreSQL (testopen.Postgres(t), testopen.PostgresIn) and SQLite (testopen.SQLite(t), through driver/sqlitedriver) as a *momo.DB for packages above the drivers, and testopen.Each runs a test once per registered dialect; there is no MySQL opener yet. A missing PostgreSQL URL fails the test when MOMO_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 and skips it otherwise (testdb does that check). testopen.SQLite skips when the build has only the stub driver (no cgo, or Windows). Tests that cannot run on a dialect skip that subtest with a stated reason. [momo-01]

docs.title: Public test kit (momotest)
docs.text: momotest is the public counterpart for applications; it is independent of internal/testdb (it does not require pgvector). momotest.New(t, opts...) returns a *momo.DB on a per-test schema momotest_<16 hex> with the project migrations applied (WithMigrations(fs.FS), run through migrate.Engine with WithoutSum), dropped in t.Cleanup after the pool is closed. momotest.NewTx(t, opts...) returns a *momo.Tx from DB.AdoptTx on a template schema named momotest_tpl_<hash of the migration files and extensions>, built once under a PostgreSQL advisory lock and marked ready with a schema comment, so a half-built template left by a killed run is rebuilt; the transaction is rolled back in t.Cleanup. momotest.Seed, Insert and Graph insert fixtures in order inside one transaction or savepoint. The URL comes from MOMO_TEST_POSTGRES_URL (WithEnv changes it), with the skip and MOMO_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 behavior of testdb. See testing.md.

docs.title: Delivery order (user decision 2026-11-04: PostgreSQL and pgvector first)
docs.text:
This is a roadmap, not a status report. Milestones are executed in this order. Tests are written once and are dialect-parameterized. The harness runs a dialect only once that dialect's driver task has landed, so a later milestone extends coverage without rewriting tests.

  1. M1: PostgreSQL + pgvector, end to end. momo-01; momo-02; momo-03 PostgreSQL tasks (pgx adapter, classification, transactions, pinned connections, COPY/batch, FromSQLDB, PgBouncer, replicas); momo-04 core engine plus PostgreSQL tasks, with engine tests running on PostgreSQL; momo-05 on PostgreSQL; momo-06 on PostgreSQL; momo-07 pgvector tasks and hybrid search; momo-09 hooks, momotest and OTel.
  2. M2: SQLite + sqlite-vec parity. momo-03 SQLite tasks; momo-04 SQLite inspection, rendering and rebuild; momo-07 sqlite-vec task. Adding SQLite to testopen.Each turns on every existing parameterized test for SQLite.
  3. M3: MySQL/MariaDB. momo-08.
  4. M4: Ecosystem, adoption, performance, docs site. momo-10, momo-11, momo-12, momo-13.

testopen.Each(t, func(t *testing.T, db *momo.DB, d dialect.Name)) runs a subtest named after each dialect available in this build. Each driver milestone adds its entry. In CI, the requirement that every dialect's URL is set (MOMO_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1) applies only to dialects whose milestone has landed.

docs.title: Ownership decisions (round 2)
docs.text:
• internal/testdb (momo-01) provides URLs only: PostgresURL, PostgresAppRoleURL, PgBouncerURL, SQLitePath, Schema, MySQL84URL, MySQL97URL, MariaDBURL. The env vars are MOMO_TEST_POSTGRES_URL, MOMO_TEST_POSTGRES_APP_URL, MOMO_TEST_PGBOUNCER_URL, MOMO_TEST_MYSQL84_URL, MOMO_TEST_MYSQL97_URL and MOMO_TEST_MARIADB_URL.
  • internal/testdb/testopen (momo-03; it imports drivers) provides Postgres(t, opts ...momo.Option) and PostgresIn returning *momo.DB, plus Each. Dialect coverage is expressed by subtests named after the dialect, never by _Postgres-style test-name suffixes.
  • internal/suite (momo-05) holds the shared feature suites, with suite.Caps and suite.CapabilitiesOf(d *dialect.Dialect) Caps.
  • Fixtures: the root momo_test package has one unit fixture, owned by momo-01 in unit_fixtures_test.go as type unitDocument. The integration fixtures live in internal/suite (suite.Document, ...).
  • Keyset pagination (After) is implemented by momo-01, including the rule that nullable keys return ErrUnsupported. momo-05 only adds integration tests.
  • Schema base types and FormatVersion belong to momo-01. The managed-object types (Namespace, View, Function, Trigger, Policy, partitions, RLS flags) belong to momo-04 Task 1. They are structured definitions, and the MomoConfig companion methods in momo-02 take the same structured arguments.
  • Cross-cutting spec tests with one owner: TestWindowsPaths (S-26) is owned by momo-04 in the CLI task. It asserts forward slashes in both the generator import/output paths (momo-02 API) and the migration file paths. Momo-01 only checks that the windows-latest CI job exists.
  • Docs pages are owned by feature plans: docs/migrations.md (momo-04), docs/vectors.md (momo-07). docs/mysql.md and docs/PERFORMANCE.md do not exist yet. momo-13 owns the site, nav and the remaining pages.

docs.title: Integration test harness
docs.text: See "Ownership decisions (round 2)". internal/testdb (momo-01) returns URLs and paths only. internal/testdb/testopen (momo-03) opens a *momo.DB per dialect and provides Each. When a URL is unset, the test fails if MOMO_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 (set in CI for every landed milestone) and skips otherwise. Only these helpers call t.Skip. Every test file that uses these helpers carries the //go:build integration tag, enforced by TestIntegrationTagConvention in internal/repocheck; untagged builds (make test, the macOS and Windows jobs) therefore contain no database test. The harness skip/require rule still decides skip versus fail inside a tagged run. CI and make test-integration always run go test -tags integration -race ./... with MOMO_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1. make db-up starts docker compose -f internal/testdb/compose.yaml up -d with pinned images.

docs.title: Per-test isolation
docs.text:
go test ./... runs packages in parallel against one server, so every test gets its own namespace and tests may use fixed table names such as docs.

  1. testdb.PostgresURL(t) connects to MOMO_TEST_POSTGRES_URL with github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 directly (not a Momo driver, so no import cycle), creates schema t_<16 hex chars from crypto/rand>, and returns the base URL with search_path=t_xxx,public (a pgx runtime parameter). It is memoized per *testing.T (sync.Map keyed by t), so testopen.Postgres(t) and raw PostgresURL(t) calls in one test share one schema; a subtest calling it with its own t gets its own schema unless it uses the parent's db. t.Cleanup runs DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE (error: t.Errorf). Once per process (sync.Once plus pg_advisory_lock(7_000_001)) it runs CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector SCHEMA public, so vector types resolve through public.
  2. PostgresAppRoleURL(t) uses the same schema as PostgresURL(t) for that t (it calls it first) and adds, run as the administrator, GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA t_xxx TO <app role>, ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA t_xxx GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES TO <app role> and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA t_xxx GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO <app role> (tables the administrator creates in that schema are covered; the app role has no CREATE, so CREATE TABLE fails with SQLSTATE 42501). The role credentials come from MOMO_TEST_POSTGRES_APP_URL, with search_path appended the same way.
  3. PgBouncerURL(t) uses the same schema and appends search_path the same way. The test PgBouncer image cannot track search_path, so a startup search_path is not reliable through the pooler. PgBouncerURLFor(t, dbname) returns the pooler URL for another database (no search_path; the pooler routes every database name) and ScratchDatabase(t, prefix) creates and later drops such a database, so the pooled shared suite runs in a scratch database of its own.
  4. SQLitePath(t) is filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "momo.db").
  5. MySQL84URL, MySQL97URL and MariaDBURL create database t_<16 hex> through github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql directly, return the DSN with that dbname, drop it in t.Cleanup, and are memoized per t.
  6. Tests never CREATE or DROP schemas or databases themselves and need not use unique table names; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS is unnecessary but harmless.
  7. Migration-engine tests that inspect the database introspect current_schema() only, unless a test explicitly manages extra namespaces. Those namespace names derive from the per-test schema name: testdb.Schema(t) returns t_xxx.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Budgets are measured, never aspirational. This page starts with the hook overhead budget that TestSelectNoHooksAllocBudget enforces. The bench/ module (a separate Go module, so GORM, Ent and Bun never enter the library's import graph) holds the comparison workloads; its methodology, versions and regression policy are added here as the suite lands.

docs.title: Hook overhead budget
docs.text:
A primary-key lookup on a database with no hooks registered must not allocate more than the budget below. The figure is allocs/op of BenchmarkSelectNoHooks, measured by the TestSelectNoHooksAllocBudget run in CI. The full CI matrix (Go 1.26 and 1.27, PostgreSQL 16 and 17 with pgvector 0.8.7) measures the same 32, so one budget covers every combination. The test fails when the measured value rises above the budget, so an allocation added to the disabled-hook path is caught. Lower the budget in the same change whenever the path gets cheaper.

Benchmark Budget BenchmarkSelectNoHooks allocs/op 32

To reproduce, run make db-up, then make bench-hooks. The benchmark opens a database, so it only compiles with the integration build tag and make bench-smoke skips it; the bench-module CI job runs make bench-hooks against the pgvector service.

docs.title: Comparison suite
docs.text: The bench/ module compares Momo with handwritten pgx and database/sql, GORM, Ent and Bun on one PostgreSQL server. Every operation is defined once in bench/workload and each library implements it in bench/adapters; the equivalence test TestBenchEquivalence fails when an adapter returns different rows than the handwritten pgx reference or leaves different state after a write, so a workload whose SQL meaning differs between libraries cannot be published.

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text:
• Identical pool settings for every adapter: 16 connections, one hour connection lifetime. The native pgx path uses the statement cache; the other libraries run on the pgx standard library driver.
  • GORM runs with SkipDefaultTransaction, as Momo adds no implicit transaction. Bun runs on the same pgx standard library database/sql handle as Ent and GORM, so the comparison isolates the ORM layer. No library cache is enabled.
  • The data is deterministic: a fixed seed, 200 customers with 5 orders each. ANALYZE runs after seeding.
  • ORM-only microbenchmarks report p50, p95 and p99 per call beside allocations, for six operations over all six libraries. A mixed read and write workload with concurrency and the bulk insert paths have their own runners.
  • Bulk insert compares chunked VALUES, COPY and Momo's Unnest, one statement with one array parameter per column, at 1000, 10000 and 40000 rows.
  • Vector search is compared at equal recall: a sweep picks the smallest hnsw.ef_search whose recall at 10 reaches 0.95 against exact search, and both the Momo builder and the handwritten statement then run at that setting.
  • Generated-code size and compile cost of the benchmark models are measured by bench/codesize.

docs.title: Pinned versions
docs.text: The module versions are pinned in bench/go.mod; each run records them in versions.txt and env.json, together with the Go toolchain, the machine, the PostgreSQL version and the pgvector version. The database image is pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg17.

docs.title: Reproducing a run
docs.text: make db-up starts PostgreSQL with pgvector. Then make bench runs the whole suite ten times per benchmark and writes bench/results/ under a directory named by UTC time, operating system and architecture, with env.json, versions.txt, codesize.json, raw.txt and summary.txt. make bench-suite-smoke runs one iteration of everything and is what CI uses. make bench-generate regenerates the Momo metadata and the Ent client.

docs.title: Regression policy
docs.text:
• Timings are judged only on a dedicated machine: a regression is flagged when benchstat reports a change above 10 percent with p below 0.05 across two consecutive full runs. Shared CI runners are too noisy for timings, so CI never gates on them.
  • Allocation counts are deterministic, so CI gates them: the bench-module job of ci.yml and ci-agent.yml runs make bench-gate, which runs the allocation benchmarks, compares allocs/op with bench/baseline/allocs.txt using benchstat and fails above 5 percent with p below 0.05. The gate runs in that one job only, against the PostgreSQL service the job already starts, so a pull request pays for one database job and not a second one. The recipe runs under bash with pipefail, and benchgate exits 2 (never 0) when the new run has no allocs/op rows or lacks a benchmark that the baseline has, so a run that never happened cannot pass. make bench-gate runs the same comparison locally and make bench-baseline rewrites the baseline.
  • Budgets are the median of the reference run plus 10 percent and are reviewed on every full run.

docs.title: Status of the published numbers
docs.text: No full run on a dedicated machine has been committed yet, so this page records no comparative timings. The only budget in force is the hook overhead budget above, which CI enforces. Timing figures will be added from the stored bench/results/ run, never from a shared runner.

docs.title: Interceptors: application-level statement rules
docs.text: An interceptor is a function attached to one *momo.DB handle with momo.WithInterceptor. It runs before the typed statements of that handle, may append predicates to them, and may deny them by returning an error. It is an application-level guard, not a privacy or security boundary: it filters only the primary table of the typed Select, Insert, Upsert, Update, SoftDelete and Delete builders, and every path listed under "What an interceptor does not cover" bypasses it. Use it to remove accidents, and use database row-level security where isolation must hold when application code is wrong.

docs.title: What an interceptor sees
docs.text:
type Operation struct {
    Kind  string      // "select", "insert", "upsert", "update", "delete", "truncate"
    Table string
    Where []Predicate // starts empty; append to it
}

type Interceptor func(ctx context.Context, op *Operation) error
  • Select, update and delete: the predicates in Where are ANDed to the statement and appear in the SQL that SQL returns and that the hooks see.
  • Insert and upsert: the interceptor runs so it can deny the statement; predicates appended to them are ignored. It runs when the statement executes (Exec, Rows), never for SQL, which for an insert runs neither interceptors nor hooks.
  • An Upsert, or an Insert with OnConflict and DoUpdate, has the kind upsert, not insert. ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE can overwrite an existing row, including a row of another tenant that shares the conflict key, and an appended predicate cannot stop it. A tenant rule must therefore deny the kind upsert or constrain it by other means (see the recipe). An Insert with DoNothing is an insert.
  • A soft delete has the kind delete.
  • Truncate has the kind truncate. It removes every row of the table, so a tenant-scoped handle should deny it; a predicate appended to it is ignored.
  • BulkUpdate is an update and keeps the predicates. Merge is an upsert when it has a matched update and an insert otherwise; a predicate an interceptor appends makes it fail with ErrValidation, because it cannot be applied without changing which rows match. Insert.Copy is an insert (deny only).
  • Interceptors run in registration order, before the typed model hooks (Meta.Hooks), so a denied statement never reaches a Before hook. The first error stops the chain and the statement; it is returned as a momo.Error of kind ErrValidation that still reaches the interceptor's own error with errors.Is. No SQL runs.
  • The predicates an interceptor adds are not a caller filter: an update or delete with no Where of its own is still refused with ErrUnfilteredMutation unless AllRows confirms it. A version-checked model update whose row is hidden by an interceptor predicate returns ErrNotFound, not ErrOptimisticLock. The count that decides between the two is a select, so your select interceptors run for it too.

docs.title: The context
docs.text: Interceptors receive the statement's context, so a tenant usually comes from ctx. SQL, which has no context argument, runs the interceptors with context.Background. An interceptor that reads the tenant from ctx sees none there: the SQL it returns shows no tenant predicate, and an interceptor that denies when the tenant is missing denies every SQL call. Inspect the statement a handle really runs through the hook events, or give the handle its tenant at construction (below) so the predicate does not depend on ctx.

docs.title: Recipe: a tenant handle
docs.text:
Build one handle per tenant (or per request) and give it the tenant predicate. The tenant comes from the handle's own configuration, so a statement cannot choose another one.

func tenantDB(drv momo.Driver, tenantID int64) *momo.DB {
    return momo.New(drv, momo.WithInterceptor(func(ctx context.Context, op *momo.Operation) error {
        if op.Table != "documents" {
            return nil
        }
        switch op.Kind {
        case "select", "update", "delete":
            op.Where = append(op.Where, DocTenantID.Eq(tenantID))
        case "upsert":
            return errors.New("upsert is not allowed on a tenant handle")
        case "truncate":
            return errors.New("truncate is not allowed on a tenant handle")
        }
        return nil
    }))
}

Inserts are not filtered by a predicate: the tenant column of a new row is the model's own value, so set it in a BeforeInsert model hook and do not trust the caller to set it. BeforeInsert runs only for Model and Models inserts: Values, ValuesRows and FromSelect inserts have no model and skip it, so a tenant handle that relies on the hook must also deny those forms, or deny inserts altogether and write through a trusted handle.

A read-only handle denies every write:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo"
)

func readOnly(drv momo.Driver) *momo.DB {
    return momo.New(drv, momo.WithInterceptor(func(ctx context.Context, op *momo.Operation) error {
        if op.Kind != "select" {
            return fmt.Errorf("handle is read-only: %s on %s", op.Kind, op.Table)
        }
        return nil
    }))
}

func main() { _ = readOnly }

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
An interceptor belongs to the handle it was registered on:

  • A transaction begun with Begin or Tx from that handle runs the same interceptors.
  • A handle created by another call to momo.New, even over the same driver, has none of them.
  • Registering an interceptor on one handle never changes another.

docs.title: What an interceptor does not cover
docs.text:
Each of these bypasses every interceptor. Scope them explicitly or use row-level security.

  • Relation loading: Load, Preload and LoadCounts query the related tables without interceptors.
  • Joined relation tables: for a Joined relation only the primary table is filtered; the joined table is not.
  • The association helpers (Link, Unlink, Replace and the like) and graph creation.
  • Subqueries and other sources rendered inside a statement: subquery operands, UPDATE ... FROM sources, and the FromSelect source of an insert.
  • Raw SQL of every kind: momo.Exec, momo.MapRows, momo.Scalars, momo.SQL fragments and momo.RawSubquery.
  • Bulk loading with COPY: Insert[T].Copy runs the insert interceptors (deny only) and BeforeInsert, but a predicate an interceptor adds is ignored, and momo.CopierOf(...).CopyFrom skips them entirely.
  • Anything run on the driver directly, and any other *momo.DB over the same driver.

For isolation that holds even when application code is wrong, use database row-level security with the transaction setup hook (WithTxSetup) and a policy on the table. Treat interceptors as the first layer and row-level security as the enforcing one.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Sensitive columns are masked in hook events: bound values of columns tagged sensitive reach hooks as momo.RedactedArg.
  • Typed model hooks (Meta.Hooks) change values on a model before a write and after a read; see the HookSet documentation for how to set them and for what a Before hook may leave behind when a statement then fails.

docs.title: Go to SQL type mapping
docs.text: This page lists which SQL column type Momo uses for each Go field type, what survives a round trip, and where the edges are. The tables are checked by tests: TestTypeMappingDoc fails when a row here disagrees with the generator's type map or a codec's SQLType, and TestTypeMapping creates a column of each documented PostgreSQL type on a live server and round-trips edge values through it.

docs.title: How a type is chosen
docs.text:
1. A field whose type implements the codec contract (types.Codec: Scan, Value and SQLType) uses its own SQLType. This is how types.TimeOfDay and types.Hstore get their columns.
  2. Otherwise the generator maps the Go type with its built-in table (package gen/typemap). A pointer and the sql.Null* wrappers map like the type they wrap: nullability is a column property, not a type property.
  3. A Go type with no mapping (for example uint64 or map) makes typemap.Map return an error wrapping momo.ErrUnsupported, which the generator reports at the field. Give the type a codec or declare the column yourself.

docs.title: Generated mappings
docs.text:
N is the size tag for string and the dim tag for vector types. A vector.Vector or vector.HalfVector field without dim is supported: it maps to the bare vector or halfvec type, a dimensionless column that holds embeddings of any size (see vectors.md). vector.SparseVector and vector.Bits require dim. SQLite has no vector types. A slice of a scalar maps to the PostgreSQL array of its element type; SQLite has no array columns, so the generator rejects them there.

Go type PostgreSQL SQLite int bigint INTEGER int8 smallint INTEGER int16 smallint INTEGER int32 integer INTEGER int64 bigint INTEGER float32 real REAL float64 double precision REAL bool boolean INTEGER string text TEXT string with size:N character varying(N) TEXT []byte bytea BLOB time.Time timestamp with time zone TEXT types.UUID uuid TEXT types.Date date TEXT types.JSON[T] jsonb TEXT vector.Vector vector(N) unsupported vector.HalfVector halfvec(N) unsupported vector.SparseVector sparsevec(N) unsupported vector.Bits bit(N) unsupported vector.Vector (no dim) vector unsupported vector.HalfVector (no dim) halfvec unsupported []string text[] unsupported []int16 smallint[] unsupported []int32 integer[] unsupported []int64 bigint[] unsupported []bool boolean[] unsupported []float32 real[] unsupported []float64 double precision[] unsupported

The PostgreSQL type of time.Time can be changed for the whole project with the types: section of momo.yaml, for example types: {time.Time: timestamp(3)} for a database created by Prisma (see naming: prisma in ai-guide.md). Only time.Time can be overridden; a type: tag on a field still wins, and SQLite ignores the setting. timestamp(3) stores a wall clock without a zone, so follow the timestamp notes below and pass UTC times.

On SQLite, bool is stored as 0 or 1, and time.Time, types.UUID, types.Date and types.JSON[T] are stored as text. The SQLite column is what the generator emits. The SQLite driver (driver/sqlitedriver, cgo, not on Windows) reads text columns back into time.Time, *time.Time, sql.NullTime, sql.Null[time.Time] and types.Date, whatever the column was declared as.

docs.title: Codec-provided mappings
docs.text:
These types are not in the generator's table. Their own SQLType method names the column; the generator's table is the fallback for everything else.

Go type PostgreSQL SQLite types.TimeOfDay time TEXT types.Hstore hstore TEXT types.TSVector tsvector TEXT types.TSQuery tsquery TEXT

types.Hstore needs the hstore extension; the vector types need vector (pgvector). Momo never runs CREATE EXTENSION for you.

docs.title: Mappings you declare yourself
docs.text:
The generator never emits these columns, but the Go types work against them when you write the DDL (or a migration) by hand. There is no SQLite column to document because nothing generates one.

Go type PostgreSQL SQLite time.Time (timestamp) timestamp n/a string (decimal) numeric n/a

docs.title: Edge values and behavior
docs.text:
Each statement below is asserted by a test against PostgreSQL.

  • Integers: math.MaxInt64 and math.MinInt64 round-trip through bigint; int is 64-bit and maps to bigint. A value that does not fit the column (an int64 above math.MaxInt16 into smallint) is a database error, not a silent truncation. uint64 has no mapping and is rejected when bound if it exceeds math.MaxInt64.
  • Floats: NaN, +Inf and -Inf are legal double precision and real values and round-trip. Compare with math.IsNaN, since NaN != NaN.
  • Strings: any valid UTF-8 round-trips, including quotes and backslashes (they are bound, never interpolated). PostgreSQL rejects U+0000 in text. A string longer than size is a database error on character varying(N).
  • []byte: nil stores NULL; an empty non-nil slice stores an empty bytea.
  • time.Time on timestamptz: the instant is preserved, the zone is not. A value written at +05:30 reads back as the same instant in the server session's location, so compare with Time.Equal, not ==. Precision is microseconds; finer digits are cut. Times before 1970 and year 9999 work.
  • time.Time on timestamp (no zone): you store a wall clock. Pass t.UTC() and treat the column as UTC; a value in another zone is stored as its UTC wall clock.
  • types.Date: stores the year, month and day of Time in its own location; it reads back at midnight UTC. Compare the date, not the zone.
  • types.UUID: round-trips all 16 bytes, including the all-zero UUID.
  • types.JSON[T]: encodes with encoding/json. An empty slice and a nil slice are different JSON ([] and null) and read back as such. Query it with JSONText, JSONPath, JSONContains and JSONHasKey. A nullable column holds either SQL NULL or the JSON literal null; an extraction is NULL for both and for a missing key, so test the column itself with IsNull. Grouping by an extraction works only for plain keys (letters, digits, underscore) and not on a sensitive column; see the AI guide pitfalls.
  • types.TimeOfDay: nanoseconds since midnight, truncated to microseconds (PostgreSQL time precision); 86399999999000 is the last representable value, and a value outside one day is an error.
  • types.Hstore: a nil *string value is an hstore NULL; keys and values with quotes and backslashes are escaped.
  • types.TSVector and types.TSQuery: the server's text form, with the lexemes sorted and normalized, so write values in that canonical form to compare them with ==. An empty tsvector reads back empty. Full-text expressions are PostgreSQL only (see docs/fulltext.md).
  • []string on text[]: elements containing commas, quotes, the text NULL, or empty strings round-trip; an empty slice reads back empty.
  • Slices as arrays: only []string, []int16, []int32, []int64, []bool, []float32 and []float64 map. []int is not mapped, because its width is platform dependent; use []int64. []string with a size tag becomes character varying(N)[]. A nil slice binds as NULL, so inserting it into a NOT NULL array column fails with a not-null violation; pass an empty non-nil slice (it stores {}), or give the column a default '{}' and omit it. The array predicates bind a nil value list as an empty array, never NULL.
  • Slices as arrays: only []string, []int16, []int32, []int64, []bool, []float32 and []float64 map. []int is not mapped, because its width is platform dependent; use []int64. []string with a size tag becomes character varying(N)[]. A nil slice binds as NULL, so inserting it into a NOT NULL array column fails with a not-null violation; pass an empty non-nil slice (it stores {}), or give the column a default '{}' and omit it. The array predicates bind a nil value list as an empty array, never NULL.
  • Decimal: carry numeric as a string to avoid binary floating point. Values beyond float64 precision round-trip exactly, and numeric also accepts NaN.

docs.title: Null handling
docs.text: A column that can be NULL needs a Go type that can hold NULL: a pointer (*int64), a sql.Null* wrapper, or a type whose Scan accepts nil. Scanning NULL into a plain int64 or into a codec from the types package is an error, never a silent zero value.

docs.title: Using these docs with an AI coding agent
docs.text: Momo is meant to be written by agents as well as people. The documentation is built so an agent can read it without scraping HTML.

docs.title: Where an agent should read
docs.text:
• Agent guide: one self-contained file with setup, modeling, migrations, queries, relations, vectors, errors, testing and the rules. If an agent reads one page, it reads this one.
  • llms.txt on the documentation site lists every page with a link to its raw Markdown. llms-full.txt contains the Markdown of every page in one file. Each page also has a raw .md twin next to its HTML. All three are generated at build time and exist under every published version of the site.
  • The repository root has its own llms.txt for agents that read the repository instead of the site.

docs.title: Canonical patterns
docs.text:
The shapes below are the ones the guide teaches. The linked examples run against PostgreSQL in CI.

  • Describe a table as a struct that embeds momo.Model, run momo generate, and build queries from the generated descriptors. See getting started and the quickstart example.
  • Insert with Insert[T] and Model, read with Select[T] and Where, change rows with Update[T] and Set, remove them with Delete[T] or SoftDelete. See crud-zero-null.
  • Run related statements in db.Tx and use the tx it passes in. See transactions.
  • Load relations explicitly with Load, LoadAll or Preload. See relations.
  • Change a schema by editing the model and running momo migrate diff, then review the SQL it wrote. See migrations.

docs.title: AGENTS.md snippet
docs.text:
Copy the block below into the AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md) of a repository that uses Momo. It is the short form of the rules in section 12 of the agent guide; a test keeps it complete.

## Momo (Go ORM)

- PostgreSQL with pgvector is the only supported database for `momo migrate`; elsewhere it is the reference database. SQLite (cgo driver, not on Windows; vectors through sqlite-vec on that driver only) and MySQL 8.4, MySQL 9.7 and MariaDB 11.8 run queries and writes, and have library migration dialects (`migrate/sqlite`, `migrate/mysql`); check docs/capabilities.md before relying on a feature there.
- Run `momo generate` after every model change and commit the generated files. Never edit generated files.
- A non-pointer model field is NOT NULL; a pointer field is nullable.
- Pass user input only as arguments to `momo.SQL`, `momo.TypedSQL`, `momo.Exec` and `momo.Scalars`. Never build SQL by string concatenation.
- Never bypass `ErrUnfilteredMutation` with `AllRows`; add a `Where`.
- Check errors with `errors.Is` against the `momo.Err*` sentinels. Never match error text.
- Use only the `tx` handle inside `db.Tx`. Retry the whole transaction on `ErrSerialization`, never inside it.
- Never edit a migration that has been applied. Write a new one with `momo migrate diff`.
- Run `momo generate --check` in CI.
- Run `momo migrate validate` in CI.
- Test against a real PostgreSQL with pgvector. Do not mock `momo.Querier`.
- Full reference: https://azrtydxb.github.io/momo/latest/ai-guide.md

docs.title: Momo guide for AI coding agents
docs.text:
Target: github.com/azrtydxb/momo v0.3.0. Read this file instead of the Momo source. Every identifier below was checked against v0.3.0. Where the guide says DON'T, the call either fails, silently does the wrong thing, or is a known bug.

Imports used throughout:

import (
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo"                    // core: DB, Tx, Select, Insert, Update, Delete, errors
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/driver/pgxdriver"   // PostgreSQL driver (pgx v5)
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/vector"             // vector.Vector, HalfVector, SparseVector, Bits
    "github.com/azrtydxb/momo/types"              // types.UUID, Date, JSON[T], TimeOfDay, Hstore, TSVector, TSQuery
    "yourmodule/models"                           // your structs
    "yourmodule/models/task"                      // GENERATED: one package per model (lowercase model name)
)

Deeper docs: README, relations, migrations, vectors, capabilities, supported versions, type mapping, architecture, examples.

docs.title: 1. Scope
docs.text:
• v0.3.0 supports PostgreSQL 16 and 17 with pgvector 0.8.x, through pgx v5; SQLite and MySQL are covered by the next bullet.
  • PostgreSQL is the reference database. SQLite is usable through driver/sqlitedriver (mattn go-sqlite3 and sqlite-vec; it needs cgo and does not build on Windows) or through the pure-Go driver/sqlitepure (modernc.org/sqlite; no cgo, no vectors, sqlitepure.Config is the same type as sqlitedriver.Config), but momo migrate exits 2 for SQLite and the vector builders work on sqlitedriver only (sqlitepure reports Vectors=false). SQLite and MySQL migrations exist as libraries (migrate/sqlite, migrate/mysql with migrate.NewEngine), not as CLI commands. MySQL and MariaDB have a driver package of their own (MySQL stores vectors only; MariaDB has distance functions); check the MySQL column of docs/capabilities.md before relying on a feature. Keep dialects: at [postgres] for generated migrations.
  • Go 1.26.10 or newer (the go.mod floor, which carries the standard-library security fixes). Pre-v1: no compatibility promise; pin the exact version.
  • Forward migrations only in the CLI. No migrate rollback, new, lint or rebase command; the Go API has Engine.Rollback and Engine.Rebase.
  • momo generate --from-db DATABASE_URL turns a live PostgreSQL database into models and an init snapshot (see migrations). Other databases: write models by hand.
  • Reciprocal-rank-fusion hybrid search does not exist. Use momo.SQL / momo.TypedSQL for it. Full-text search (types.TSVector, momo.TSMatch, momo.TSRankCD, momo.TSHeadline, the query builders) exists on PostgreSQL; combine it with a vector distance in one score as shown in fulltext.md.

Details: capabilities.md. Example: quickstart.

docs.title: 2. Install and tooling
docs.text:
go get github.com/azrtydxb/momo@v0.3.0                # adds the library to go.mod and writes go.sum
go install github.com/azrtydxb/momo/cmd/momo@v0.3.0   # the CLI: generate, migrate, help

Run go get first in a fresh module: it produces go.sum, which go run and the generated code's compilation need. go install puts momo in $(go env GOPATH)/bin; make sure that is on PATH.

Layout of a project (the models package holds structs; momo generate writes into it):

go.mod
momo.yaml
models/models.go          # yours
models/momo_gen.go        # generated (MomoMeta for each model). Commit it.
models/task/momo_gen.go   # generated: columns and relations of Task. Commit it.
migrations/               # momo migrate diff writes here. Commit it.

Minimal momo.yaml (at the module root; the CLI finds it by walking up to go.mod):

version: 1
packages:
  - ./models
dialects: [postgres]
migrate:
  dir:
    postgres: migrations
  url_env:
    postgres: DATABASE_URL

naming: is optional: momo (default: snake_case columns, plural snake_case tables), gorm, bun, ent, prisma. Pick one and never change it: a change renames columns.

naming: prisma matches a database that Prisma created: the table is the model name as written and quoted (KbChunk), the column is camelCase (createdAt, accountId; an ID word at the end becomes Id, and a trailing IDs becomes Ids, so UserIDs is userIds), and the constraint and index names are <Table>_pkey, <Table>_<col>_fkey, <Table>_<col>_key (unique) and <Table>_<col>_idx. Those names come out of the table and column names, so no tag is needed for single-column keys and indexes.

Limits of the preset:

  • A composite @@index or @@unique is named by Prisma from all its columns (<Table>_<a>_<b>_idx). Name such an index explicitly in MomoConfig or with an index:/unique: tag name.
  • The implicit many-to-many table is named _AToB (model names in alphabetical order), but its A and B columns and its foreign key names are not reproduced. Declare that table with an explicit join model instead.
  • A column name that does not follow the camelCase rule needs a column: tag.

Prisma maps DateTime to timestamp(3), so add a types: section:

naming: prisma
types:
  time.Time: timestamp(3)

types: overrides the default PostgreSQL column type of a Go type. Only time.Time is supported, and the value must be timestamp, timestamptz, time or timetz with an optional precision 0-6 and an optional with/without time zone (anything else is refused, as it is written into DDL). A type: tag on a field still wins. It applies when the first entry of dialects is PostgreSQL (or dialects is empty); with SQLite first it is ignored. Without it time.Time is timestamp with time zone.

Generate:

//go:generate momo generate

momo generate            # writes *_gen.go
momo generate --check    # CI: exit 1 and "stale: <path>" lines when stale; writes nothing

Rules:

  • DO run momo generate after every change to a model struct or tag, before compiling code that uses the generated packages.
  • DO commit generated files. DON'T edit *_gen.go and DON'T name your own files *_gen.go (the generator refuses to overwrite non-generated files).
  • DO put *_gen.go text eol=lf in .gitattributes if anyone uses Windows, or --check reports CRLF files as stale.
  • DON'T use go run of the CLI inside app code; the library (momo) never imports the generator.

Details: README "Configure and generate". Example: quickstart.

docs.title: 3. Connecting
docs.text:
func openDB(ctx context.Context, url string) (*momo.DB, func(), error) {
    pool, err := pgxdriver.NewPool(ctx, url) // (ctx, string) (*pgxpool.Pool, error)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    return momo.New(pgxdriver.New(pool)), pool.Close, nil // New(pool, opts ...Option) momo.Driver
}
  • The caller owns and closes the pool. momo.DB has no Close.
  • *momo.DB is safe for concurrent use; create one at startup and share it.
  • DSN: postgres://user:password@host:5432/dbname?sslmode=verify-full. Use sslmode=disable for local development only. Momo adds no TLS options; pgx reads sslmode, sslrootcert, ... from the URL.
  • Read the URL from the environment, never hard-code credentials.
  • Pool sizing: Momo documents no recommendation and sets nothing. pgxpool options (for example pool_max_conns=N in the URL) apply. Each open Tx, WithSearch block, Replace and CreateGraph holds one connection for its whole duration.

Other constructors:

sqlDB, drv := pgxdriver.FromConnConfig(cfg, opts...) // cfg *pgx.ConnConfig; returns (*sql.DB, momo.Driver)
drv = pgxdriver.FromSQLDB(sqlDB)                     // sqlDB must be backed by pgx stdlib; for an existing *sql.Tx see SQLTx, AdoptTx and UnwrapSQLTx in section Transactions

database/sql paths have no Batch or COPY path (relation loading falls back to sequential statements; correct, just slower).

PgBouncer (transaction pooling):

  • pgxdriver.New defaults to pgx.QueryExecModeExec (unnamed statements, server-side binding). That is PgBouncer-safe; set nothing.
  • pgxdriver.WithExecMode(m) accepts pgx.QueryExecModeCacheStatement, pgx.QueryExecModeCacheDescribe, pgx.QueryExecModeDescribeExec (import github.com/jackc/pgx/v5; not tested through PgBouncer). The simple protocol is rejected with ErrUnsupported on every query. DON'T select it.
  • With FromConnConfig set cfg.DefaultQueryExecMode = pgx.QueryExecModeExec first; pgx defaults to CacheStatement, which is NOT PgBouncer-safe. Its opts have no effect.
  • DON'T run momo migrate through a transaction pooler (section 5).
  • Set search_path per role or per transaction, not at connection startup.

Details: capabilities.md "Getting connected", supported-versions.md "PgBouncer".

docs.title: 4. Modeling
docs.text:
A model is a struct that embeds momo.Model BY VALUE. The tag on that embedded field names the table. The tag grammar is momo:"opt,opt:value,..."; a value cannot contain a comma. An unknown, duplicate or malformed option is a generator diagnostic and nothing is written for that package.

type Account struct {
    momo.Model `momo:"table:accounts"`
    ID         int64      `momo:"pk,identity"`
    Email      string     `momo:"size:200,unique"`
    Plan       string     `momo:"size:20,default:'free',index"`
    Note       *string    `momo:"size:500"`                         // pointer = nullable
    Balance    int64      `momo:"default:0"`
    Version    int64      `momo:"version,default:0"`                // optimistic lock
    CreatedAt  time.Time  `momo:"column:created_at,created_at"`     // set by Momo on insert
    UpdatedAt  time.Time  `momo:"column:updated_at,updated_at"`     // set by Momo on update
    DeletedAt  *time.Time `momo:"column:deleted_at,soft_delete:timestamp"`
    Embedding  vector.Vector `momo:"dim:1536"`                      // pgvector column

    Posts []Post `momo:"has_many,fk:AccountID"`
}

Nullability and column rules:

  • A non-pointer Go field is NOT NULL. A pointer (*string), a sql.Null* type, or the nullable tag makes the column nullable. notnull is redundant for non-pointers and a diagnostic on pointers.
  • A nullable field generates momo.NullColumn[T] (has SetNull()); a non-nullable one generates momo.Column[T] (SetNull() does not compile).
  • A primary key must not be nullable.
  • Scanning NULL into a non-pointer field is an error. Use pointers for nullable columns.
  • Go type to column type: see TYPE_MAPPING.md (int is bigint, string is text, string with size:N is varchar(N), time.Time is timestamptz, types.UUID is uuid, types.JSON[T] is jsonb). uint64, maps and unknown types have no mapping: add type:<sql> or a codec.
  • JSON columns: JSONText, JSONPath, JSONContains and JSONHasKey (file expr_json.go) are typed predicates over a types.JSON[T] column; the extractions are string expressions usable in Where, OrderBy and Columns. An extraction is NULL for a missing key and for JSON null alike, a SQL NULL column is tested with IsNull on the column, and the JSON literal null is matched by comparing the column with a types.JSON whose value is nil. JSONHasKey is true for a key whose value is JSON null. A numeric key in JSONText or JSONHasKey is an object key; only JSONPath elements made of digits can be array indexes. SQLite renders json_extract and json_type (JSONContains is ErrUnsupported there); MySQL renders its JSON functions.
  • Column names default to the naming preset (CreatedAt becomes created_at). Fields are exported only; a tag on an unexported field is a diagnostic. Skip a field with momo:"-".

Tag reference (all lower case):

Tag Meaning table:<name> (on momo.Model) table name; always set it. Also schema:<name>. pk primary key; several pk fields make a composite key (a tag belongs_to target needs a single-column key) identity database-generated identity (GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY) serial PostgreSQL smallserial/serial/bigserial id by Go int width (sequence owned by the column, DEFAULT nextval); omitted from inserts and read back with RETURNING like identity; excludes identity and default; refused on other dialects column:<name> column name size:<n> varchar(n); strings only precision:<p>, scale:<s> numeric precision (float, decimal, or a string without size that carries a numeric); scale needs precision dim:<n> vector dimension; optional on vector and halfvec (none: dimensionless column), required on sparsevec and bit, invalid elsewhere default:<sql> column default, raw SQL (default:now(), default:'free', default:0) unique / unique:<name> unique index (single column) index / index:<name> index; modifiers sort:asc\|desc, nulls:first\|last, method:<m> need index or unique idgen:<name> client-generated string id (cuid, uuid, ulid or a name registered with WithIDGenerator); filled on insert when the field is empty version optimistic-lock column (integer type) created_at[:unix\|unixmilli\|unixnano], updated_at automatic timestamps; field type time.Time, *time.Time, int64 or *int64 soft_delete:timestamp\|unix\|bool soft-delete marker; Go type *time.Time, *int64 or bool read_only, create_only, immutable write permissions: never written; written on insert only; never updated sensitive excluded from the generated ColumnByName allowlist (use for secrets) type:<sql>, collate:<c>, check:<expr>, comment:<t>, enum:<name> raw column type, collation, check, comment, enum type embedded, prefix:<p> flatten a named struct-typed field into this table (anonymous embedded structs flatten by themselves); prefix prepends to its column names nullable, notnull explicit nullability (rarely needed)

MomoConfig for what tags cannot express: composite or partial indexes, vector indexes, checks, enums, views, triggers, policies. The generator reads this method statically and never runs it; arguments are &receiver.Field pointers and string literals only.

func (a *Account) MomoConfig(c *momo.Config) {
    c.Unique("accounts_email_plan_key", &a.Email, &a.Plan)
    c.Index("accounts_plan_live_idx", &a.Plan).Where("deleted_at IS NULL")
    c.Index("accounts_embedding_hnsw", &a.Embedding).
        Method("hnsw").
        Opclass(&a.Embedding, "vector_cosine_ops").
        With("m", "16").With("ef_construction", "64")
    c.Check("accounts_balance_nonneg", "balance >= 0")
}

An index name declared in MomoConfig must not collide with an auto-named <table>_<col>_idx produced by an index tag (the Plan field above already yields accounts_plan_idx); the generator refuses the duplicate.

Config methods: Index, IndexExpr, Unique, Check, Enum, Default, Comment, Collate, View, Function, Trigger, Policy, RLS, Partition, PartitionOf. Index chain: Where(pred), Method(m), With(k, v), Opclass(field, op), Desc(field), Nulls(field, "first"|"last"), Concurrently() (diff writes the index as CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in its own no-transaction migration).

Many-to-many needs join: with the same table on both models you declare it on (the reverse side is optional, but if declared it must carry join: too):

type Document struct {
    momo.Model `momo:"table:documents"`
    ID         int64 `momo:"pk,identity"`
    Title      string
    Tags       []Tag `momo:"many2many,join:taggings"` // join table taggings(document_id, tag_id)
}

type Tag struct {
    momo.Model `momo:"table:tags"`
    ID         int64 `momo:"pk,identity"`
    Name       string
    Documents  []Document `momo:"many2many,join:taggings"` // optional reverse side, same join table
}

Relation tags (a relation is an exported field of struct, slice or pointer type; it is not a column):

Tag Field type FK lives on Notes belongs_to,fk:<Field> *Target this struct fk names the FK field on THIS struct; make it a pointer if the relation is optional has_one,fk:<Field> *Target the target fk names the field on the TARGET has_many,fk:<Field> []Target the target fk names the field on the TARGET many2many,join:<table> []Target join table set join: (same table) on every side you declare; the reverse side is optional; two key columns <model>_<pkcol>

Extra relation options: polytype:<column> + polyvalue:<value> (both, on has_one/has_many only: polymorphic), on_delete: / on_update: (cascade, restrict, set_null, set_default, no_action; they affect only the FK emitted for belongs_to), no_constraint (emit no FK). has_one and has_many create no FK constraint themselves; the belongs_to on the other side does. Many-to-many join tables get a composite primary key plus two FKs with ON DELETE CASCADE.

Generator diagnostics (nothing is written for the package until fixed): more than one relation kind on a field; field type does not match the kind; target is not a Momo model; fk missing or naming a missing field; many2many without join:, or a declared reverse side without join:; polytype without polyvalue (or the reverse), or on a kind other than has_one/has_many; polytype column not a field of the target; many-to-many to the model's own type; momo.Model embedded by pointer; a generic model; size on a non-string; dim on a non-vector; sparsevec or bit field without dim; scale without precision; notnull on a pointer; nullable primary key; unknown tag option; Go type with no SQL mapping.

What the generator emits per model Task (package task):

  • task.Table (a momo.TableRef), one column variable per field (task.ID, task.Title), task.As("t") for aliased columns, task.ColumnByName(name) and task.ColumnNames() (an allowlist for user-supplied sort/filter names).
  • One momo.Relation[Parent, Child] per relation field (document.Comments, document.Author).
  • Vector fields become momo.VectorColumn[vector.Vector] (nullable: NullVectorColumn).
  • read_only / create_only / immutable fields become permission-typed columns that have no Set (or insert-only Set).
  • Package name = lowercase model name. It can collide with your local variable names (task := ... shadows the package). Name variables differently or alias the import.

docs.title: Client-generated ids
docs.text:
Databases that keep ids as text and generate them in the client (Prisma @default(cuid())) have no column default to lean on. Declare the generator on the field, with the tag or in MomoConfig:

package main

import "github.com/azrtydxb/momo"

func main() {}

type Contact struct {
    momo.Model `momo:"table:contacts"`
    ID         string `momo:"pk,idgen:cuid"`
    Name       string
}

type Note struct {
    momo.Model `momo:"table:notes"`
    ID         string `momo:"pk"`
}

func (n *Note) MomoConfig(c *momo.Config) { c.IDGen(&n.ID, "ulid") }
  • Built-in generators: cuid (25 characters in the layout Prisma writes, so old and new ids look alike), uuid (random, version 4, 36 characters) and ulid (26 characters, sortable by creation time). Register your own, or replace a built-in, with momo.New(drv, momo.WithIDGenerator("short", fn)) and tag idgen:short. Names are lowercase; the MomoConfig form takes a string literal.
  • The generator fires when an insert writes the field and it holds the Go zero value: Model, Models, Upsert and every chunk of a bulk insert. An id you assigned is kept. The generated id is stored in your struct (the model you passed, or the slice element), so read m.ID after Exec or Rows.
  • The field must be a string kind (named string types and *string work). Any other type, a name given twice (tag and MomoConfig) or identity/serial on the same field is refused by the generator. A name that is neither built in nor registered fails the insert with ErrValidation.
  • A column named in Omit always takes a fresh generated id, which is bound and written back like any other. Values and ValuesRows that leave the id out get one too. SQL() shows a generated id in the arguments but does not store it in the model.
  • On an OnConflict upsert whose target is not the primary key, the row in the database may keep its own id. Exec then asks the database for the stored id and writes that into the model (a DoUpdate that hit an existing row gives that row's id). A model whose row DoNothing skipped keeps the id it had, usually empty. This needs RETURNING; without it (MySQL) the id is not written back for such statements. Rows never writes back there: read the id from the returned rows.
  • When the id is written back up front (every statement except the conflict case above), it stays in your struct also when the insert fails. Retrying the same struct reuses the id, and so do all rows of a failed chunked insert. Clear the field to get a new one. In the conflict case the model is updated only after a successful statement.
  • In the conflict case, rows are matched to models on the conflict-target columns (or on the generated id for DoNothing without a target), so those columns must read back exactly as you wrote them; citext, char(n) and numeric columns may not. A returned row that matches no model fails with ErrValidation and the write is rolled back; only a pinned OnConn handle, which cannot open a transaction, keeps it. If two models share a target value, the first one is matched. A non-primary-key generated column (such as a public_id) counts as a conflict case too, because the kept row has its own; the default DO UPDATE set of Upsert leaves such a column out, so a conflict never replaces the stored value, even one you assigned; to overwrite it, pass an explicit DoUpdate that sets it.
